subject: Sample independence  and standardized covariates in distsamp

messages.author: 732a31c2f861aaca
messages.subject: Sample independence  and standardized covariates in distsamp
parts:
Unmarked users I wanted to pose the question of whether I should be
concerned with the issue of dependence among samples if I am using 1km
square grid with 16 points spaced at 250 meters apart and treating
each point as an independent sample using the distsamp function. I
was not sure if the hierarchy of the unconditional maximum likelihood
would treat this point dependence appropriately. Does the latent
density parameter integrate out the dependence among points?

Another question I had with regards to predicting density throughout
my study area is that when using standardized variables how valid is
it if the standard deviations obtained from the study area are much
different from the model (sampled data). I would think that if a
model is fit using standardized variables the betas are using a
different standard deviation scale than the covariates obtained when
predicting to the rest of the study area. I hope this made sense.

Thanks for any help with this.

Rob

messages.author: df74d6fccec2ff7e
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Sample independence and standardized covariates in distsamp
parts:
Hi Rob,

Do you think that abundance at one point influences abundance at another point? If not, you probably satisfy the independence assumption. If so, the model will not likely fit the data very well, which should be revealed by a goodness-of-fit test. If there is some sort of dependence in your data, unmarked won't help you much until we develop some spatial model, which we're working on...

I don't really understand your second question. There should not be any problems associated with standardizing your covariates. You just need to back-transform your predictions appropriately, as has been discussed in another thread.

Richard

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Sample independence and standardized covariates in distsamp
parts:
hi Rob
(1) I think 250 m is probably close enough to independent for most
birds. As usual, even moderate amounts of dependence shouldn't have
much affect on things and even in severe cases should only bias the
SEs of parameters.

(2) The SD that you use the standardize the covariates will almost
certainly be different from the population SD but that doesn't matter
as long as you use that same value to standardize the covariate values
that you use to make predictions on. e.g., if xbar = 2.5 and sigma=.73
for some covariate so that you did this:
xstd<- (x-2.5)/.73
then if you have a new set of covariate values to make predictions
then you need to use the same values:
xnewstd<- (xnew-2.5)/.73

regards
andy
